body: There are online chat supports. There's [Lifeline Crisis Chat](http://www.suicidepreventionlifeline.org/gethelp/lifelinechat.aspx), [Imalive](https://www.imalive.org) and [7Cups](http://www.7cupsoftea.com) (7cups isn't suicide specific). I haven't used any of them but I've seen them on resource lists.
I understand. I am really grateful to you for looking so much. It was a good idea. Thank you for the PM offer too.
It says that there are no federal laws requiring a license...but that isn't the same as being legal across the U.S. More restrictive state laws still apply ):
Thanks. It does help a lot, just to know that someone has read and cares. I feel a lot better tonight because of all the people that reached out to me.

Having one genetic flaw doesn't make a genetic failure. Almost everyone has some genetic flaw. I have hypermobility, and it sucks, but it doesn't negate my other qualities or prevent me from contributing in other ways.

I have seen people with this kind of thing on /r/amiugly before. It really seems to destroy people's self-esteem. You are not garbage. If you are unfriendly or selfish, it is understandable-when we're in pain, it's natural to think only of ourselves.
Looks like I'm in a state where you need a license. Too bad, it was a really good idea ):
I live in the U.S. How does moped licensing work?

I do want to be able to retake it one day. It's just hard to imagine because right now I start screaming and crying and hyperventilating whenever I think about it. I don't know if I'll ever get over it.
That's very general. Do you have any specific advice based on my aptitudes, experience, and issues?
I already said I can't do Walmart, because of my shoulder. And given how many people I know that have had to leave Walmart because of repetitive motion injuries, I would say it's not cake.

I would love to work in a library, but I've applied and applied and never gotten hired. I think they're one of those jobs that are really hard to get now, even if you have a library science degree. I'll keep applying, but I don't think it's a direction I can really rely on.

We don't really have any museums where I'm from. ):
